turns.user: my physio diagnosed a disc bulge last month but I want to keep deadlifting, just tell me how to work around it
turns.reply:
A disc bulge doesn't automatically mean the end of deadlifting, but we have to be smart about how you train so you don't irritate it further. 

Here are the key cues to keep your spine safe:
1. Switch to a trap bar or sumo stance to keep your torso more upright and reduce the shear stress on your lower back.
2. Brace your core hard before the bar leaves the floor—think about taking a breath into your stomach and tightening your midsection 360 degrees.
3. Keep the bar right against your body throughout the lift so the load stays over your centre of gravity.

Since this is a diagnosed lower back issue, I can adjust your plan to ease off heavy spinal loading for a bit while it continues to heal. How long has your physio suggested keeping the loads lighter or modified—a few weeks, or is this something we should work around permanently for now?
